title: Reactive vs Proactive
summary: Reduce repetitive reactive work with AI to create space for proactive tasks.

sections.heading: Orientation — What Will You Understand?
sections.subtitle: What Will You Understand?
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What Will You Understand? Repetitive tasks that require your response every day consume your thinking time — AI (artificial intelligence) can help reduce some of this.
- Why Now? In the previous lesson, you identified a recurring decision. Today, you will understand why the same decisions come up every week and keep you in a 'firefighting' mode.
- What After the Lesson? You will list 5 weekly tasks and categorize them as Reactive or Proactive — and choose one reactive task that AI can help reduce.

sections.heading: Tension — A Familiar Situation
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown: You end your day feeling like you've been 'busy' — but nothing has been built. A business owner opens WhatsApp in the morning — supplier, client, employee, complaint. By 3 PM, they find themselves still responding. No time for pricing or planning. This is Reactive mode: the world dictates your day — not you. It's not laziness — it's the repetition of unorganized work. AI does not solve all problems. However, it helps with repetitive tasks: summarizing, drafting responses, prioritizing — freeing up half an hour for Proactive work each week.

sections.heading: Core Idea — The Main Concept
sections.subtitle: The Main Concept
sections.contentMarkdown:
Reduce the Repetitive — Open the Door to Proactive - Reactive: Tasks that come to you — messages, problems, urgent requests. They need to be done, but they do not build the business on their own.
- Proactive: Tasks you choose — pricing, new proposals, following up with important clients, improving processes. This is what drives the business forward.
- If 90% of your week is reactive, you won't build a system. The goal is not to have zero reactive tasks — the goal is to reduce the repetitive with AI so that proactive work becomes possible.
- Ask yourself: 'What task do I do every week in the same way?' — this is the first candidate for AI.

sections.heading: Glossary — Two Terms for Classification
sections.subtitle: Two Terms for Classification
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| Reactive | A task that comes to you from outside — you must respond or act immediately | Client complaint, supplier message, urgent request from an employee |
| Proactive | A task you plan for before it becomes a crisis | Reviewing weekly numbers, updating price lists, designing follow-ups for clients |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: Karim opened WhatsApp early in the morning due to a major supplier issue and spent 3 hours. What is this?
Reactive — the situation dictated his day before he could choose his priorities.
Explanation: The size of the problem is not the measure. The measure is: who decided what to do first? Reducing the repetitive starts with knowing when the 'world' takes your day.
bullets: Reactive — the situation dictated his day before he could choose his priorities.

sections.heading: Mission — Your Task (Intent + MSA Draft Labels)
sections.subtitle: Your Task (Intent + MSA Draft Labels)
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: The task is practical — not motivational. Write down 5 tasks you do every week (or almost), and categorize each one as Reactive or Proactive. Then choose one reactive task that AI can help reduce. Full automation is not required — honest diagnosis is needed. Submission: The five tasks + categorization + selected reactive task + how AI helps (one or two sentences). Evaluation Criteria ( : | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-----------|--------|----------|

| AI Selection | 40% | One reactive task with a specific idea for assistance |
